description: Replace the linear-to-zero Muon learning-rate decay with a cosine decay 0.5*(1+cos(pi*step/total)), leaving the SGD bias and head schedules linear.

Extend the uncertain-subset TTA in infer's _get_tta_logits from three base views (original plus two shifted crops) to four shifted corner crops (tl, tr, bl, br at pad=1), each with its flip, so the average is over 8 views as specified; the original unshifted image is dropped to reach 8 views.
Raise the Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation in the Muon step from 3 to 5 iterations by adding two more copies of the A/B/X update before the transpose-back in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5.
Add an identity shortcut around conv2 in ConvGroup, enabled only when channels_in equals channels_out (so only block3's 256-to-256 group), with the BatchNorm still unscaled.

Adds a linear warm-up over the first 3% of total_train_steps to the lr_factor2 multiplier used for the Muon learning rate (and the other lr_factor2 groups), leaving the existing linear decay in place.
Raise the random translation from 2 to 3 pixels (7 crop offsets per axis instead of 5), leaving the test-time TTA pad at 1 because its conditional change cannot be decided before the run.

Trains the first 40% of steps on batches bilinearly downsampled (antialiased) to 24x24, with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so the network works at both sizes, to cut early-step time at similar accuracy.

issues: I found no attempt to get around the measurement. The diff adds no state that carries from one run to the next, does not seed any generator, does not touch the test images, and has no file access or new imports. F.interpolate comes from torch.nn.functional, which the script already uses.

The architecture change is safe. With 32x32 input, the final feature map is 3x3, so AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) gives the same result as MaxPool2d(3). With 24x24 input the map is 2x2, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) is what still reduces it correctly to 1x1. predict() still runs at full 32x32 resolution, and the last 60% of training also runs at 32, so training and evaluation stay consistent.

Training at 24x24 means torch.compile builds a second graph for that shape. The untimed warmup call runs the same schedule, so both shapes should already be compiled before timing starts. This is allowed, because only compiled code carries over. If the warmup did not reach both shapes, recompilation would only make the timed runs slower, which would count against the candidate, not for it.

I can't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's run-to-run sd is not given. The candidate mean is -0.1428. Using the stated per-job noise sd of 0.026 with 2 candidate runs and 15 incumbent runs, the standard error is about 0.0196, giving z of about 7.29. That agrees with the reported 7.351.
A gain of about -0.14 is large, but progressive resizing is a known speedup, and both runs agree (-0.147 and -0.138). The claim matches the numbers. It is still worth adding replicates.

description: Trains the first 40% of steps on batches bilinearly downsampled (antialiased) to 24x24, with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so the network works at both sizes, to cut early-step time at similar accuracy.

Remove the leading nn.GELU() applied to the whitening output in self.layers, saving one elementwise kernel per pass; the whitening pairs (w, -w) keep sign information linearly, though GELU before conv1 is a real nonlinearity, not a redundant one, so accuracy may drop.

Ramp LABEL_SMOOTHING linearly from 0 at the first step to its full value at the midpoint of training, then hold; the smoothing is passed into the compiled forward_step as a preallocated CUDA tensor, with the cross-entropy written out by hand so it accepts a tensor.

Replace the alternating whole-dataset flip with an independent per-sample random horizontal flip applied each epoch via the compiled batch_flip_lr, applied to the padded images (equivalent under reflect padding), keeping translate and colour jitter unchanged and EPOCHS fixed.
Replace the SiLU activation in ConvGroup with a squared-ReLU module (relu(x).square()), leaving the input GELU, the rest of the network, and the schedule unchanged.

The crash is a finiteness check, not a shape error: predict produced NaN or inf logits in eval mode, most likely from BatchNorm dividing by a near-zero running variance under half precision with the tiny eps=1e-12. Raising eps to a half-representable 1e-5 (the PyTorch default) should keep the normalisation finite; this is a best-guess fix that has not been run.

Stop the alternating-epoch horizontal flip once step reaches 80% of total_train_steps, by un-flipping odd-epoch batches inside train() from that step on, while translation and brightness/contrast jitter stay on.

Pre-shuffled epoch tensor: permute the augmented images and labels once per epoch and slice contiguous batches, instead of gathering each batch by index. Not submitted: the expected gain is below the noise floor.

issues: Integrity check passed. The diff only replaces the global max pool with a concatenation of max pool and average pool, and widens the head input to 2*block3. Nothing carries over between runs, nothing is seeded, the test images are not used and no files are accessed.

No bug that would void the result. The head input dimension matches the concatenated features (512). The new module has no parameters, and the .half() loop covers the head. One minor caveat: the head's output scaling and learning rate were tuned for 256 max-pooled features. The average-pooled half shifts the logit scale, which probably explains part of the loss in quality, but that is a legitimate design result.
The numbers are consistent with rejection. The candidate's cost is -0.0281 against an incumbent mean of -0.1427, so the candidate is worse by about 0.115 in cost.

Recomputed z = (-0.1427 - (-0.0281)) / (0.026 * sqrt(1 + 1/2)) ≈ -3.60. The harness reports -3.629, which implies a slightly smaller standard error (about 0.0316) and is the same within rounding of the noise sd. The decision to reject stands.

description: Replace the final AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with a module that concatenates spatial max and mean pooling (512 features), and widen the head to nn.Linear(2*block3, 10, bias=False), keeping the /x.size(-1) scaling so it adapts to the new feature count.
Disable brightness and contrast jitter from the start of the epoch containing step 0.8 * total_train_steps, leaving flip and translation unchanged.
Set nesterov=False in the Muon optimizer constructed in train() so the orthogonalised update uses the plain momentum buffer, testing whether Nesterov look-ahead helps at this learning rate.
Self-distillation from a mid-run frozen teacher snapshot, mixing 0.5 smoothed labels with 0.5 teacher softmax for the second half of training (not run).

Ramp the Muon momentum linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to MUON_MOMENTUM (0.655) at 10% of total training steps, then hold it there, by updating the Muon param group's momentum before each optimizer step.
Raise WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 1.0 so the whitening-layer bias trains for the first full epoch before freezing, with BIAS_LR and its linear decay unchanged.

Drops the confidence-based top-25% selection in predict's tta function so the flip and shift ensemble (_get_tta_logits) runs on every test image in fixed 2000-image batches, removing the initial pass and topk.
